name: Combobox
description: The APG editable combobox over a list of your own rows: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/

props.name: data
props.description: Every row the combobox can offer. Filtered by the query unless `filter` is `false`.

props.name: def
props.description: How to read a row: its `label` (the text, which is searched and read out), its `key` (what makes two rows the same row), and optionally `disabled` and `display`. A key of the row, or a function.

props.name: label
props.description: The combobox's name, rendered above it in a real `<label>`. A combobox is not named by what it contains, so without this (or an `aria-label` of your own in `props`) it has no accessible name.

props.name: labelProps
props.description: Styles for the `<label>` itself — it sits above the control rather than wrapping it.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The field's placeholder. Not a name — it is gone on the first keystroke. See `label`.

props.name: name
props.description: What the selection submits under: one hidden input per selected row, carrying its key.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Not editable and not openable, but still read out. The real attribute, on the field itself.

props.name: props
props.description: Attributes for the `<input>` that *is* the combobox — an `aria-label`, an `inputMode`, an `id`.

props.name: itemsProps
props.description: Styles for the popup (`combobox.items`).

props.name: hideIcon
props.description: Drop the chevron. It is decoration either way: `aria-hidden` and never focusable.

props.name: filter
props.description: Which rows a query leaves, and in what order — it takes the whole list so it can rank as well as reject, and is handed the label reader so composing it with the built-in one costs nothing. `false` means the data is already filtered, which is what a server that searched needs.

props.name: loading
props.description: Rows are on their way. The popup says so rather than claiming there are none.

props.name: loadingText
props.description: What the popup shows while `loading` and there is nothing to show yet.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: What the popup shows when the query matched nothing.

props.name: createRow
props.description: Turns the query into the row it would create, or `null` to refuse it. Its presence is what offers a create row at all, and one is never offered for a query a row already answers by name.

props.name: createLabel
props.description: What the create row reads. Given the query, since the row it would make is not the one shown.

props.name: virtualize
props.description: Render only the rows on screen, which is what a list of thousands needs to open in one frame. On by default above a hundred rows; an object tunes it (`threshold` is what turns it on earlier), `false` never windows and `true` always does. Rows have to be a uniform height for it, which is measured rather than declared — a `display` that varies one wants `false`.

props.name: removeLabel
props.description: A chip's remove button's accessible name, given the row's label.

props.name: query
props.description: The typed text. Controlled — pair it with `onQueryChange`, which is also the hook an async search uses.

props.name: defaultQuery
props.description: The text the field starts with when the combobox owns its own query.

props.name: onQueryChange
props.description: Fires with the text and why it changed. Only `input` came from a keystroke.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the listbox is showing. Controlled — pair it with `onOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether it starts open, when the combobox owns that itself.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires with the new state and why: a press, a keystroke, a choice, Escape, or a press outside.

parts.name: Combobox (single-select)
parts.description: One row at a time, which is the default: the value is a row or `null`, and the field shows the selected row's label whenever nothing is being typed.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Leave it off, or `false`. See the multiple half for the other shape.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected row, or `null`. Controlled — pair it with `onValueChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: What is selected to begin with, when the combobox owns its own value.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with the row itself — the object out of `data`, not a key dug out of it — and why.

parts.name: Combobox (multiple)
parts.description: Several rows, shown as chips in front of the field, and the value is an array. Choosing a row that is already chosen takes it off again, which is the keyboard's way to a chip its own button cannot reach.

props.name: multiple
props.description: `true` is what turns the value into an array — the one shape a combobox cannot read off its value.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected rows. Controlled — pair it with `onValueChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: What is selected to begin with, when the combobox owns its own value.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with the whole selection, as rows, and why it changed.

keyboard.action: Types, which opens the listbox and filters it. Filtering never moves the highlight: that is list autocomplete, not inline, and a highlight nobody asked for gets committed.
Opens, or moves the highlight through what the filter left, wrapping and skipping disabled rows.
Opens without moving the highlight. Alt + Up — chooses and closes.
Move the caret, and hand the highlight back to the field.
Chooses the highlighted row. With nothing highlighted it does nothing, so a typed query is never committed by accident.
Closes the listbox, keeping what was typed. Pressed again on a closed one, clears it.
Commits the highlighted row, then moves on. Nothing is highlighted until an arrow key put it there, so this only ever commits a deliberate choice.

a11y: The `<input>` carries `role="combobox"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"` and `aria-expanded`; the popup is `role="listbox"` with `role="option"` rows, named by `aria-activedescendant` rather than by focus, so one Tab enters and one leaves however many options there are.
Nothing names a combobox for you: pass `label`, or an `aria-label` in `props`.

A chip's remove button is deliberately not a tab stop — twenty selections would otherwise cost twenty presses to Tab past. Backspace on an empty field removes the last, and the listbox toggles a row back off, so removal is reachable from the keyboard without them.
The popup is a sibling of the field in the browser's top layer, so it needs no portal and keeps the theme, the custom properties and the direction around it.
